Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya Patel, AE at Redwood, joining with Leo my SE. Quick run through agenda, then a live demo of the Hosted API for chat and text generation, focus on streaming, parameters and retries.
[00:12] Dr. Kim: Thanks, Maya. We're looking at generating clinical summaries from EHR notes, low latency is critical. Happy to hear about streaming.
[00:20] Jamal: Also want to understand quota and cost, we run thousands of notes/day.
[00:25] Maya: Totally. Briefly, Redwood's hosted API gives you text generation, chat, embeddings; you can stream partial tokens to keep latency low and show progressive results to users. We'll demo both the non-streaming and streaming paths.
[00:38] Leo: Quick note, from an infra perspective we also expose model catalogs and performance profiles so you can pick faster quantized variants for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:46] Priya: On security, are logs retained? How do you handle keys, and do you support customer-managed KMS?
[00:53] Maya: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations for dedicated and private deployments; for hosted we have SOC 2, encryption at rest in transit, and configurable retention. I'll share the security pack after the call.
[01:05] Maya: Ok jumping into the demo. I'm switching to the console — here is the API quickstart: a simple POST to /v1/chat with messages array. Example: {"role":"system","content":"You are a clinical summarizer"} then user note.
[01:20] Maya: Non-streaming call: you set max_tokens and temperature; lower temperature (0-0.3) for deterministic summaries. Example python snippet: client.chat.create(model="redwood-1", messages=..., temperature=0.2, max_tokens=250).
[01:40] Leo: For cost-savings we recommend controlling max_tokens and using prefix caching if notes share common boilerplate. Optimize will surface batching suggestions — e.g., group short notes into a batch if latency SLO allows.
[02:05] Maya: Now streaming. Switch streaming flag to true and the server will send incremental chunks. We use server-sent events; your client can render partial text while generation continues.
[02:20] Dr. Kim: How does streaming interact with stop sequences? If model emits a stop mid-stream what happens to event stream?
[02:28] Leo: Stream sends a final event with done=true; clients should handle partials and finalize when done flag arrives. For stop sequences you still get partial tokens until the stop triggers closing the response.
[02:45] Jamal: What about retry logic? We have transient 429s under load.
[02:50] Maya: Good question. We recommend exponential backoff plus jitter for 429s and 5xx. Also use idempotency keys for non-streaming requests that mutate state (or to prevent double processing). For streaming, best to design the client to resume from last stable checkpoint or re-request with a cursor if you persist partial tokens server-side.
[03:12] Priya: Any guidance on concurrency and rate limits with hosted?
[03:16] Leo: Hosted has per-account rate limits; we can provide committed throughput (Dedicated) if you need guaranteed QPS. For hosted, we suggest client-side pooling and batching for short notes to reduce per-token cost.
[03:28] Maya: Demoing the SDK retry helper now — here's a snippet that wraps requests with a retry policy: 429 or 503 triggers backoff, max attempts 5, base delay 200ms with factor 2 and jitter.
[03:45] Maya: Also show how to set streaming with SSE in curl: curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat?stream=true" -d '{"messages":[...]}' . You get a sequence of data: events with delta chunks.
[04:05] Alex: Is there a transcript of the generated text or is it only token stream?
[04:09] Leo: You get both: streaming events are deltas; the final response includes the assembled text and metadata like model, tokens, token_count.
[04:20] Maya: On parameters: temperature controls randomness, top_p controls nucleus sampling. For clinical summarization we usually recommend temperature 0-0.3 and top_p 0.8-1.0. max_tokens should be tuned to expected summary length.
[04:40] Jamal: How do you measure token usage and cost?
[04:44] Maya: Console shows token-level cost breakdown by request, model, and route. You can export usage to CSV and set alerts. Optimize can recommend a smaller model or quantized profile if quality is acceptable.
[05:00] Dr. Kim: Any automated quality monitoring? We need to detect hallucinations/regressions.
[05:06] Leo: Yes, Redwood Optimize integrates evals and prompts; you can define prompts/tests and get alerts on quality drift when model updates or rollout changes affect metrics.
[05:18] Maya: Quick note on function/tool calling — useful if you want structured outputs. You can declare a JSON schema and the model will return structured payloads; reduces post-processing.
[05:30] Priya: For PHI, we need data residency in us-east. Is that supported on hosted?
[05:36] Maya: We have regional hosting options and can provide dedicated regions; for stricter requirements Private (VPC) or Dedicated with on-prem are options. I'll flag this for the security pack.
[05:50] Jamal: Performance question: what's typical latency for a 250-token summary?
[05:54] Leo: On hosted with the recommended model it's ~150-250ms/token depending on concurrency; end-to-end for 250 tokens typically 1.5-3s when streaming. We can run a benchmark during POC on your data.
[06:10] Dr. Kim: If we hit a regen edge case (client asks for regen), what's the idempotency recommendation?
[06:15] Maya: Use idempotency keys for server-side operations; for pure generation we recommend client-side dedupe and store the original request parameters so you can re-run deterministically (low temp) or record the model output.
[06:28] Alex: Can we get a simple integration example for our Node service?
[06:33] Leo: Sure — I'll include Node and Python samples, plus streaming client code. Also sample backoff/retry helpers.
[06:40] Maya: Ok, quick recap: we'll send pricing and security docs, Leo will share benchmarks and code snippets, Jamal will confirm POC dataset and SLOs. Proposed POC: 2 weeks, run batch of 5k notes/day with streaming UI and evaluate latency and clinical accuracy.
[06:59] Dr. Kim: Sounds good. Priya we'll loop in legal on retention.
[07:04] Priya: Yes please, also need an RCA for data flows.
[07:08] Maya: Noted. Any last questions?
[07:12] Jamal: One small thing — do you support pinned model versions and rollbacks?
[07:16] Leo: Yes, you can pin model versions per route and use rollouts/canaries. Console shows traces per version for regression analysis.
[07:25] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items we discussed.
